Keep NPO due to fatigue; start IV fluids as prescribed.

Prepare for high-flow nasal cannula therapy.
Avoid routine bronchodilators unless provider-directed trial shows response.

patient.name: Ethan Howard

ehr.overview: Young adult admitted with splinted tibia/fibula fracture.

Prepare for possible fasciotomy.
Continue neurovascular checks every 15 minutes.

diagnostics.result: Paresthesia present; dorsalis pedis pulse palpable; lower leg tense and firm.
Capillary refill 2 seconds; numbness improved; wound vac in place.

Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiac monitoring.
Prepare repeat naloxone or infusion if recurrent respiratory depression occurs.
Assess for withdrawal and safety when awake.

end_of_case_debrief.clinical_judgment_map: High spinal cord injury, severe headache, hypertension, bradycardia, sweating/flushing, and bladder distention led to autonomic dysreflexia management.
end_of_case_debrief.missed_cues: A weaker learner may treat headache with analgesics while missing severe hypertension.
end_of_case_debrief.priority_trap: The trap is lying the client flat or delaying trigger removal.
end_of_case_debrief.safety_lesson: Autonomic dysreflexia can cause stroke or seizure if severe hypertension persists.
end_of_case_debrief.outcome_interpretation: BP and headache resolved after bladder drainage, but recurrence prevention is essential.
end_of_case_debrief.next_time_rule: SCI above T6 plus pounding headache equals check BP and bladder now.
